children: NHTSA opened an audit of about 1,000 Tesla (TSLA) Cybercab vehicles, seeking technical data on certification and whether omission of pedals, steering wheel and mirrors meets FMVSS compliance.
Tesla (TSLA) began limited public Cybercab robotaxi rides in Austin with ~45 vehicles. Two-seat, wheel-free AI camera-driven system; Tesla cites 1M+ unsupervised miles while NHTSA reviews safety.
TSLA fell 5.6% the day of Tesla’s Cybercab event. The company didn’t livestream or give extra details. Cybercab rides were set to open to the public at 5 p.m. CT Friday.
Regulators limit non‑compliant self‑driving vehicle exemptions to about 2,500 units yearly. Tesla (TSLA) faces similar regulatory limits and legal hurdles for robotaxi deployment.
Tesla (TSLA) vehicles on road use Full Self‑Driving v14; reports suggest Cybercabs may run FSD v15 and include SpaceX Grok AI and Starlink broadband.
Analysts gave mixed reactions to Tesla (TSLA) after its event: critics called details vague and no live stream; others still see robotaxi upside and potential scale cost cuts; price targets vary.
JPMorgan said a SpaceX IPO could make an all-stock merger with Tesla (TSLA) more feasible, citing strategic fit, shared engineering and battery ties, while noting regulatory and governance hurdles.
Investor Gary Black called Tesla's Cybercab reveal a bust, citing sparse details and unanswered questions on planned deployment numbers and regulatory risk over no steering wheel or pedals.
Analyst Gordon Johnson keeps Sell on Tesla (TSLA) with $24.86 target after Cybercab event, citing unresolved production scale, pricing and governance questions and ~93% implied downside.
